query: evidence that older methods for For the class-matched detections in one capture, select_stage2_subset ranks that DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements. It applies that strategy by the first-maximum rule std::max_element already uses, so a tie keeps the earlier candidate and the later tied candidate stays deferred. It admits at most the count the caller passes, in that rank order, and places every candidate it does not admit into deferred, preserving their order in the candidate list. Each candidate keeps its source_index. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors, admitted and deferred. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty, and an unknown strategy throws. The pose node calls it with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 still estimates that single admitted pallet. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices are written on PalletPoseStamped after input_depth_stamp. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the split is this capture while the scene can still change. When the estimate fails, publish no PalletPoseStamped and write the same two lists on the failure diagnostic, which is the only result that path publishes. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are. The user named which detections are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. The part they did not name is that the split is these two admission vectors, ordered by that first-maximum rule, on the pose result the handling process reads. have been superseded
findings: Publishing only the strict first maximum, and dropping every other detection, superseded passing the whole Detection2DArray into the pose stage. NVIDIA's Detection2DArrayFilter, copyright 2024, selects one object by class id and confidence. It replaces the running detection only when hypothesis.score is strictly greater than the current maximum and the class matches, so a tie keeps the earlier detection. If that maximum stays 0 it returns and publishes nothing. The output is one Detection2D. Isaac ROS FoundationPose builds the stage-2 mask from the highest-scoring detection in the array and publishes vision_msgs/Detection3DArray. The filter takes no caller count, stores no array slot, and does not return the detections it did not publish. An unknown selection strategy is not a case it throws on.

Greedy non-maximum suppression that returns only the kept indices superseded an unfiltered box list, and Soft-NMS superseded hard deletion of overlaps. Neither leaves the boxes it does not keep in input order. OpenCV GetMaxScoreIndex, present in 3.4.20 and on 4.x, keeps a score only when it is strictly above the threshold, stable-sorts those pairs descending so an equal score keeps the earlier index, then resizes to top_k and drops the tail. NMSFast_, which cites Piotr Dollár's EdgeBoxes, writes only the surviving indices. Bodla, Singh, Chellappa, and Davis, ICCV 2017, say greedy NMS sets an overlapping score to zero and misses an object inside the overlap threshold; Soft-NMS decays the score so that step eliminates no object. OpenCV softNMSBoxes still picks with max_element and a comparator that treats the larger index as smaller on an equal score, swaps the chosen pair to the front, and appends only indices that stay above the threshold.

Throwing away every box below a score threshold before the next stage was superseded for tracking by a high-set and a low-set. Zhang et al., ByteTrack, ECCV 2022, say trackers that keep only boxes above a threshold throw away occluded objects. BYTE puts score greater than tau in D_high and the rest in D_low, associates the high set first, then associates the low set with tracks the first pass left unmatched, and deletes the tracks that stay unmatched. The output is tracks with boxes and identities. It is not the admitted source index and the other source indices of this capture, in candidate order, on a pose.

Choosing one pallet inside the current view superseded positioning a single pallet and ignoring the stack, and a language prompt superseded a detector that cannot tell loads apart. Both still omit the pallets they do not choose. Meng, Ren, Yu, Yin, Wang, and Men, Sensors 2024, 24(16):5330, say most research positions a single pallet and ignores stacks. They keep centers inside a width window, WP/2 minus WT through W minus WP/2 plus WT, and a depth window, D minus DF through D plus DB, then apply unloading priority, and for a stack the upper pallet is the target. The published result is that one pallet in the forklift frame. Lang2Lift, Nguyen et al., arXiv:2508.15427v2, selects among multiple pallets with a language prompt. Florence-2 returns boxes and scores; SAM-2 runs on each box whose score is above theta_conf and the highest quality score becomes M_best; FoundationPose is called once on that mask. The other boxes are not stored as source indices. A tie on that quality score is not specified as the earlier detection.

Returning every localized pallet, reordered, has not been superseded by an admitted prefix plus a deferred remainder in candidate order, and a 6D pose for each detected bin has not been superseded either. ifm getPallet still returns up to 10 pallets. The default palletOrder is scoreDescending, and the other orders are z or y, ascending or descending. Pixels outside the projection volume are discarded. palletIndex is a template type, 0 through 9. PalletDetection is a header plus pocket poses and has no source_index and no deferred list. Wu and Demeester, ICPRAM 2026, initialize FoundationPose from the detector boxes and write a 6D pose for each pallet bin; their collected set is one bin, so that paper does not show a deferred index list. geometry_msgs/PoseStamped is a header and a pose. Detection2D.id may be empty and is an id across messages, not the slot in this array. sensor_msgs/Image says the header stamp should be the acquisition time of that image. DiagnosticStatus carries level, name, message, hardware_id, and KeyValue pairs. No fetched source puts the admitted source index and the order-preserving deferred source indices on the pose the handling process reads, or repeats those two lists on the failure diagnostic when no pose is published.
